name: cyclopts-954e72e1-blind20-ots
instr:
# Diagnosing cyclopts without a test suite

I've been upgrading an internal tool built on this library for writing command-line programs, and I pulled a build that misbehaves in a lot of unrelated places. The repository has received 20 separate undocumented edits. My own code did not change and neither did the way I invoke anything. Everything below is what I reproduced from the outside; I have not read the source.

Assembling a program out of subcommands is the biggest of it. When I attach one by naming a module plus the name of the object inside it, so that the module is only imported if that subcommand is actually used, nothing about it works. If the target really does carry the name I attached it under, invoking it fails as though the two names disagreed, and pointing at a target whose name differs is accepted silently. Everything that depends on it is wrong too: settings that should be inherited from the parent when unset aren't, ones I set explicitly on the deferred entry get overwritten, name transforms set on the parent aren't applied, an invalid keyword in the declaration no longer raises the error it used to, an explicit description string isn't honoured, its own on-screen summary comes out wrong, and nested subcommands declared this way are missing from the generated shell-suggestion script. One deferred entry also gets pulled in when I invoke a different subcommand altogether, which it never used to. Subcommands attached the ordinary eager way are entirely fine.
